output.summary: An evergreen hardwood tree or shrub native to coastal forests and Sierra foothills of California, extending into southwestern Oregon and northwestern Baja California. Its bruised leaves smell strongly of camphor, and its purple-ripening fruit resembles a miniature avocado. Native Americans ate briefly ripe flesh and traditionally roasted the inner pit before eating it.
output.edibilityNote: Ripe flesh was eaten fresh or dried; pits were traditionally roasted before eating. Leaves have culinary use but contain high levels of toxic umbellulone.
